long_description: Nabla is an enterprise ambient AI scribe designed for health systems and multi-specialty practices—not therapy-focused documentation. The platform serves 85,000+ clinicians across 150+ healthcare organizations, processing 20 million annual encounters in 35+ languages. Key differentiator: patient audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. Nabla Connect enables rapid EHR integration via SMART on FHIR. Mental health templates cover basic documentation but may not include all MSE domains or structured risk assessment fields. Solo psychiatrists doing routine medication management may find Nabla workable, but therapists needing modality-aware notes (CBT, DBT) should use therapy-specific tools like Mentalyc or Upheal. Pricing is not public; reported at ~$119/month individual, $299-399/provider enterprise.

faqs.q: How much does Nabla cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Nabla no longer publishes pricing. Reported rates are ~$119/month for individuals and $299-399/provider/month for enterprise contracts. A sales conversation is required. A free tier exists (30 encounters/month) but BAA availability is not confirmed.

No. Nabla was designed for hospital systems and multi-specialty practices, not therapy. It doesn't understand therapy modalities (CBT, DBT, psychodynamic) and its mental health templates may lack MSE domains and risk assessment fields. Therapists should use Mentalyc or Upheal instead.
No. Patient audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. This provides strong privacy guarantees for HIPAA and GDPR compliance.
Nabla supports 35+ languages including Arabic, Mandarin, Spanish, French, Hindi, Vietnamese—making it suitable for diverse patient populations and international telehealth.

faqs.q: Does Nabla's free tier include a BAA?
faqs.a: BAA availability on the free tier is not confirmed. Using an AI scribe on patient encounters without a BAA is itself a HIPAA compliance gap. Verify with Nabla before clinical use on the free tier.
